title: How to schedule a meeting?
en:
*Convert the timezone for them*

When you provide your availability, make it easy for others to decide and plan their days by converting the time slots into their time zones.

title: How to schedule a meeting?
en:
*List specific goals of your meeting*

Tell them how the meeting can help you. Write down questions that you will ask. Describe the homework you have done. Provide background material on what you want to discuss.

Assure them that you will not waste their time.

title: How to schedule a meeting?
en:
*Send out calendar invite asap*

If an event is not on the calendar, it does not exist. 

When you finalize the time, please send a calendar invite with a detailed title/content/links as soon as possible. Also, send a reminder before the meeting on what they should expect.

title: How to schedule a meeting?
en:
Most people are generous with their time to help others. 

Following these tips will increase the likelihood of people meeting you and help you achieve your goals!
How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?

title: How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?
en:
How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?

Your curriculum vitae (Latin for "course of life") is the most important document 📜 for all sorts of career opportunities. But not all students have access to resources for learning to write a good CV.

Check out the thread 🧵below!

title: How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?
en:
*Include a photo of yourself?*

Be aware of the culture differences when it comes to including a headshot photo in your CV. It may be standard in your regions (e.g., Europe, Asia), but it's weird if you are applying positions in US and UK (for anti-discrimination reasons).

title: How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?
en:
*Add hyperlinks*

It's 2021. Don't treat your CV as a plain text document. Add hyperlinks throughout your CV and make it easy for the readers to learn more about you and your work, e.g., personal website, email, project page, paper link, videos, and code on GitHub.

title: How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?
en:
*Make good tables*

Tables are great for presenting structured data (e.g., your education/work history). But spend some time learning to make a one.

title: How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?
en:
*Provide context*

Include background information to help the readers (e.g., admission committee) understand your achievement. Some examples: rank X (out of how many)? GPA X (equivalence in 4.0 scale?), accuracy of 95% (on what task? and how well does baseline work?).

title: How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?
en:
*Describe your work*

In each of your project, talk about (1) what the problem is? (2) what did you do? and (3) what the impact/results are? Most of the time (3) is missing. It's hard for people to judge the significance of your work without (3).

title: How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?
en:
*Pick a good LaTeX template*

Pick a visually pleasing template to work with. Usually there is no page limit for your CV. Don't sacrifice readability by squeezing contents into 1-2 pages.

title: How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?
en:
*Self-rate skills?*

Listing your skills is fine, but I don't really know what "4.2 stars Python" or "3.5 stars C++" on your CV mean.

title: How to prepare your Curriculum Vitae?
en:
*Seek feedback*

Many student-led organization offer help to review and provide feedback on your CV and other application material (particularly for graduate school applications). Check them out before you submit the application!
How to find a research internship?

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
How to find a research internship?

Doing an internship helps 
• expand your network 🕸️, 
• explore new topics 💡, 
• learn new research skills 🔬, and
• earn more money 💰!

But how can we find good internship opportunities? 🤔
A thread 👇👇👇

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
*Find a supportive advisor*

Choose an advisor that encourages/supports/allows students doing summer internships. Some may require you to work on funded projects during the summers or delay graduation should you do internships. 

Reach out to prior students and learn more!

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
*Stay connected*

Many internship opportunities are not broadcasted through public posting, but via emails among faculty members. Stay connected so that you get the best info (e.g., ask your friends/advisor forward relevant posting).

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
*Get on Twitter*

There are many great internship (or jobs) opportunities advertised on Twitter.

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
*Apply broadly*

You never know whether your expertise/interest match one of the teams in industrial labs (as their focuses may vary dramatically each year). 

Remember, you cannot get an offer from a position you did not apply to!

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
*Apply early*

Most of the positions are accepted *on a rolling basis*. If you apply late, you may find that most of the positions have been filled already. 😔

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
*Send cold emails*

If you find researchers whose interests match yours very well, don't be shy and send them cold emails!

More on cold emails: https://x.com/jbhuang0604/status/1420611695848869892

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
*Content*

Your email should contain the following four elements. 

• Greeting: "Hello"
• Introduction: "My name is Inigo Montoya."
• Context/Connection: "You killed my father."
• Call for action: "Prepare to die." https://t.co/VewkqaudhH

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
*Extend and finish your project*

Summer went by very fast. Very ofter you will need a few extra months to finish the work and turn it into a good paper. 

This involves your advisor's support, company policy (e.g. code/data release or IP), and immigration issues (e.g. CPT).

title: How to find a research internship?
en:
Happy Interning! 

Best of luck with your applications!
How to intern?

title: How to intern?
en:
How to intern? 

Research internships are great opportunities to do cool research in industrial labs! But it's definitely not easy to complete a solid work in 3 months. 

Some tips for having a successful internship ... 🧵

title: How to intern?
en:
*Get ready*

Reach out to your mentors *before* starting your internship.
• understand what the topics will be 
• get yourself familiar with the literature
• reminder your mentors to iron out a detailed internship plan

👉 Make sure that you hit the ground running!

title: How to intern?
en:
*Pitch ideas*

Research internships work best when they align with your thesis topic well. How do you make this happen? 

👉 Pitch your own ideas to your hosts.

title: How to intern?
en:
*Set SMART goals*

Don't use internship for random exploration of research ideas, you should have Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound goals.

👉 Work with your hosts early on to set SMART goals and create a clear roadmap.

title: How to intern?
en:
*Help your mentors help you*

Your mentors want you to succeed! 

👉 Help them do so by communicating well. 

More: https://x.com/jbhuang0604/status/1418407079077842944

title: How to intern?
en:
How to do research with my mentors effectively? 

I get this question frequently in my open office hours. I am still learning as well but I hope sharing my ✌💰 may be helpful to some.

Key idea ➡️ **Help them help you!**

How? Check out the thread 🧵

title: How to intern?
en:
*Beyond the summer*

It's common/normal that you cannot finish up the project in 3 months. Engage with your advisor and get their support. Int'l students: plan this early as you may be delayed by logistics (e.g., part-time CPT).

👉 Finish strong!

title: How to intern?
en:
*Meet new people*

Aside from working on your project, grab lunch together with your fellow interns, attend talks, engage and ask questions, hang out with new friends over the weekends. 

👉 You will find that the connections you built are *far more valuable* than your project.

title: How to intern?
en:
Happy interning!

Wish everyone a fun and productive summer!

title: How to intern?
en:
*Own Your Project*

Remember that you are a *Research Scientist Intern*. You are there to learn and demonstrate independent research capability and collaborate with others. 

👉 Act like a research scientist, not a student who just follow instructions.
How to find research opportunities?

title: How to find research opportunities?
en:
How to find research opportunities?

Finding opportunities to gain experience is arguably the most challenging part for students wishing to pursue grad school, particularly for those who don't have resources/connections.

Some tips on approaching potential mentors. 🧵

title: How to find research opportunities?
en:
*Lead with value*

❌ "I am very interested ... I want to grow ... I want to get the experiences... I have many prior experiences ... me, me, me, me, me, me, me!"

✅ "Here is what I can contribute to your team. I can do this bc my experience/skills on blah blah blah."

title: How to find research opportunities?
en:
*Go the extra mile*

❌ Generic email sent to 500 professors. "I found your project X inspiring."

✅ "I ran the code from your latest project X. Here are some limitations I found. I think we can explore this and that direction to tackle the problem."

title: How to find research opportunities?
en:
*Make it easy to say yes*

❌ "I want to work with you this semester. Can we schedule a one-hour zoom meeting to tell me what project I can work on?"

✅ "I want to work on problem X. Here is the doc of initial explorations and my plan. Would you give me some feedback?"

title: How to find research opportunities?
en:
*Show your work (in public)*

❌ A resume of a long list of various projects you work on. 

✅ A website documenting your work at different stages (as code, report, slides, poster, video, paper).

title: How to find research opportunities?
en:
*Do the best work you can (when you have an opportunity)*

❌ Do an 8-week internship dip. Collect the "experience". Move on to yet another research opportunity. 

✅ Work hard. Complete and document your project. Doing good work naturally leads to many more opportunities.

title: How to find research opportunities?
en:
Hope this helps! And hope everyone gets their dream opportunity to learn and grow.

Best of luck!
